newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - GISSA sees growth in 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GISSA sees growth in 1997-98.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Industrial Saltillo (GISSA) sees strong growth this year and next, a top company official said on Thursday.

"Investors always want two things: profitability and growth," Felipe Mellado, the director general of the company, told Reuters in an interview. "We've been giving them one, profitability, and now were going to provide the other, which should help stock prices."
GISSA, based in the northern Mexican city of Saltillo near Monterrey, is an industrial holding company that makes white goods, auto parts and other metallic pieces for industrial use.
The group reported net profits of 473 million pesos in 1996, up 91.6 percent from 1995.
Mellada said the most important pending project for GISSA is a $65 million plant to build diesel monoblocks, which is expected to come on line by the end of 1997.
The plant will increase GISSA's annual molten iron capacity to 240,000 tonnes from 180,000 tonnes and contribute heavily to GISSA sales in 1998, he said.
"We'll then have a very significant diversification, building iron and aluminum pieces for gasoline and diesel motors that will make the division less vulnerable in the future," Mellado said.
GISSA currently holds 11 percent of the U.S. market share for monoblocks for gasoline engines with a chance to grow, Mellado said.
"We're very much interested in the U.S. market, we are investing for the U.S. market, and we're going to continue investing for the U.S. market," he said.
